newsitem.title: USA: Teva gets tentative FDA ok for pain drug.
newsitem.headline: Teva gets tentative FDA ok for pain drug.

text.p: Teva Pharmaceutical Industries Ltd said Monday it has received tentative approval from the Food and Drug Administration to manufacture and market ketorolac tromethamine tablets. Teva's tentative abbreviated new drug application is the first approval of a generic version of this product.
Ketorolac tromethamine is a generic equivalent of Roche's Toradol, indicated for severe acute pain. The patent on Toradol expires on May 16. Toradol has annual U.S. sales of aboaut $45 million.

Teva is Israel's largest pharmaceutical company, with three quarters of its sales outside Israel, mainly in the United States. The company develops, manufactures and markets branded and generic human pharmaceuticals, bulk pharmaceutical chemicals, medical disposable and veterinary products.
